## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating. All other components inspected during this visit are in good condition, but the pump failure prevents normal system operation.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet, which is normal for a tank operating at design capacity.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (1250 gal, concrete) | Good | Baffles intact; no structural defects observed |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Light soiling; cleaned and reseated during this visit |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 hp, 115V) | CRITICAL | Amp draw 1.6A / nameplate 7.2A = 22.2% FLA. No load detected. |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Pump Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no ponding or breakout observed |

## PUMP DIAGNOSTIC
The effluent pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic resistance -- a critical condition. Possible causes include:
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-run condition (no fluid in pump chamber)

Without fluid circulation through the pump, the motor cannot dissipate heat and is at risk of thermal damage. The pump must be inspected and repaired or replaced immediately.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL -- Immediate professional attention required:**
- Inspect the effluent pump discharge line for disconnection, blockage or damage. If the line is intact, the pump impeller must be inspected for breakage or separation. Do not operate the system until the pump is repaired or replaced. Continued operation risks motor failure.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is restored to normal operation.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious problem that must be fixed before your system can treat and disperse wastewater. The pump motor is overheating because it has no load to cool it. Do not delay -- contact a septic service technician immediately to inspect the pump and discharge line.

### Tank Solids
Your inspection revealed solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time as bacteria break down waste. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, medications -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable. Once your pump is repaired, the system will resume normal operation.
